lines.trans: Listen, Oguzok, come here to me.
Yes, chef! What needs to be done?
Go to the bar and bring cognac.
Which cognac exactly do you need?
I wrote the name on this piece of paper.
And what if someone notices me?
Go to the bar to keep up appearances.
And what should I say to bartender Kostya?
Say that this is for meat sauce.
Understood, I will do everything quickly and quietly.
And stuff the fish with julienne and lemon.
Then put it into the hot oven.
Right away, chef, I'm already running!
Go to the bar and bring cognac.
I wrote the name on this piece of paper.
Go to the bar to keep up appearances.
And stuff the fish with julienne and lemon.
Listen, Oguzok, come here to me.
Yes, chef! What needs to be done?
Go to the bar and bring cognac.
Which cognac exactly do you need?
I wrote the name on this piece of paper.
And what if someone notices me?
Go to the bar to keep up appearances.
And what should I say to bartender Kostya?
Say that this is for meat sauce.
Understood, I will do everything quickly and quietly.
And stuff the fish with julienne and lemon.
Then put it into the hot oven.
Right away, chef, I'm already running!
Nobody must find out anything.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'bar, pub' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Our bar is closing.

examples.text: Проверьте все бары и старых друзей.
examples.trans: Check all the bars and old friends.
It is already morning. Our bar is closing.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'bartender', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Бармен наливает холодную воду в стакан.
examples.trans: The bartender pours cold water into the glass.
The bartender poured the wine.

examples.text: Бармен, принесите нам бокал белого вина!
examples.trans: Bartender, bring us a glass of white wine!

meanings.en: to run (in one direction), to flee, to escape
meanings.note: irregular mixed conjugation: бегу, бежишь, ..., бегут

examples.trans: Run, Marina, before it's too late!
Where are you running so fast?

examples.text: Надо бежать! Беги в деревню к маме.
examples.trans: You need to run! Run to the village to your mum's.

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'slip of paper'.

examples.trans: He wrote the number on a slip of paper.
This piece of paper has no legal power.

examples.text: Такую бумажку можно купить в любом переходе.
examples.trans: You can buy such a paper in any underpass.

meanings.note: the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.trans: He drives fast.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

examples.text: Давай работай быстрее, гости уже давно ждут заказ!
examples.trans: Come on, work faster, the guests have been waiting for their order for a long time!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
Secondary conversational sense ('that's it, done') (at the start of a sentence) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
That's it, bye!

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: 'закрывать глаза на' + accusative = to turn a blind eye to

examples.text: Я не буду закрывать на это глаза.
examples.trans: I'm not going to close my eyes to this.
She has blue eyes.

examples.text: А я глаза на это закрывать не буду. Я подниму людей!
examples.trans: Well, I'm not going to close my eyes to this. I'll rally people!

meanings.en: hot (to the touch, of food/drink, not weather)
meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hot').

examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea.
Careful, the cup is very hot.

examples.text: Аркаша, держи горячий чай. И бутерброд с вареньем ешь.
examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea. And eat a jam sandwich.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh yeah?
Yes, it's me.
Oh yeah? When?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.
This is for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)
Secondary conversational sense ('owe') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I have to work.
Greed should be moderate.

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'oven'.

examples.trans: Can you believe it, they forgot it in the oven!
The pie is in the oven.

examples.text: Представляешь, в духовке забыли! Юль, выйди.
examples.trans: Can you believe it, they forgot it in the oven! Yul, step out.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?

examples.trans: Come if you want.
And if not?
Take her if you want.

meanings.note: baked dish of mushrooms, cheese, and cream

examples.trans: Cook a delicious julienne.

examples.text: И фаршируй рыбу жюльеном с лимоном.
examples.trans: And stuff the fish with julienne and lemon.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'метить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to notice', forming an aspectual pair with 'замечать'.

examples.trans: He did not notice the loss.

examples.text: Никто на кухне ничего не заметил.
examples.trans: Nobody in the kitchen noticed anything.
And what if someone notices me?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: вот именно = that's just it, quite right
Secondary conversational sense ('namely') (а именно = namely) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Exactly, quite right.

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

examples.text: Вот именно. Но мне сдаваться нельзя.
examples.trans: Exactly. But I must not give up.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'to' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.
I'm going to Mum's.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('what') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.trans: What is your town like?
What a beautiful house!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: genitive also 'коньяку' (some cognac)

examples.trans: He drinks French cognac.
The cognac is very expensive.
And you're drinking French cognac yourself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('someone') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.trans: Finally someone is for the people!

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

examples.text: Ты что, не понимаешь? Я задавить кого-то мог!
examples.trans: Don't you understand? I could have run someone over!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'lemon', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Add a slice of lemon.

examples.text: И фаршируй рыбу жюльеном с лимоном.
examples.trans: And stuff the fish with julienne and lemon.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('meat (attributive)').

examples.trans: Meat dishes are very filling.

examples.text: Но сочные мясные котлеты такие вкусные!
examples.trans: But juicy meat cutlets are so tasty!

examples.text: Скажи, что это для мясного соуса.
examples.trans: Say that this is for meat sauce.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: name, title (of an object, place, or dish)
meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'звание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'name, title' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I wrote the name on a piece of paper.

examples.text: Я написал название на этой бумажке.
examples.trans: I wrote the name on this piece of paper.

examples.text: Ты просто изменил старые названия на новые!
examples.trans: You simply changed old names to new ones!

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'писать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to write', paired with 'писать'.

examples.trans: He wrote a statement.
Write to me.

examples.text: А зачем? Я сам сделал так, чтобы он его написал.
examples.trans: And why would I? I'm the one who made him write it.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: needs 'не' with the verb: никто не войдёт

examples.trans: Nobody will come in.
I know the town like nobody else.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('nothing') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('never mind, it's okay') (as a reply on its own) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Never mind, never mind.
I don't know anything.
I didn't understand a thing, Arkash.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.
You need to rest.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: short form 'нужен / нужна / нужно / нужны' + dative: 'мне нужна работа' = I need a job

examples.trans: I need a job too.
Do you need a pen?
He needs money.

meanings.note: playful derogatory nickname used by Chef Barinov for Max

examples.trans: Runt, are you still standing here?
The chef often called the newcomer a runt.

examples.text: Огузок, ты официально принят в штат нашего ресторана!
examples.trans: Rump, you are officially hired onto our restaurant staff!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.trans: She's a lecturer.
I haven't heard of her.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: chiefly used in the idiom для отвода глаз

examples.trans: This is needed to keep up appearances.

examples.text: В бар сходи для отвода глаз.
examples.trans: Go to the bar to keep up appearances.

meanings.en: to come up to, to approach
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ойти'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to come up', forming an aspectual pair with 'подходить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to suit, to fit') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Come here to me!
Keep away from my child!

examples.text: Нам не нужна ваша приставка! Ещё раз подойдёте к моему ребёнку — пожалеете!
examples.trans: We don't need your console! Come near my child again and you'll be sorry!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to understand', forming an aspectual pair with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: I didn't understand.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

examples.text: Ты точно понял, как нужно правильно нарезать этот стейк?
examples.trans: Did you definitely understand how to slice this steak properly?

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'then'.

examples.trans: First coffee, then work.
I'll call later.
And then waste will flow.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нести'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to bring (carrying)', paired with 'приносить'.

examples.trans: What did you bring into the flat?
He brought you a dog.

examples.text: А я вот вам чаю с сушками принёс.
examples.trans: I've brought you some tea and bread rings.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'fish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: A big platter of fish and crabs.

examples.text: На ужин мы приготовили свежую рыбу.
examples.trans: For dinner we cooked fresh fish.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to do', forming an aspectual pair with 'делать'.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
I'll do it tomorrow.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Secondary conversational sense ('tell me / tell us') (polite request) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: What did you say?
Excuse me, where's the metro?
Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to listen', forming an aspectual pair with 'послушать'.
the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'
Secondary conversational sense ('hello (on the phone)') ('Слушаю' = I'm listening) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Listen, Samson.
Yes, I'm listening.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушаться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to obey', forming an aspectual pair with 'послушаться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: Understood, chef!
Understood, chef! I will find the knife.

examples.text: Слушаюсь, шеф, я сделаю всё моментально.
examples.trans: Understood, chef, I will do everything instantly.

meanings.note: culinary condiment or liquid topping

examples.text: Паста под соусом была очень вкусной.
examples.trans: The pasta with sauce was very tasty.
The chef prepared a spicy tomato sauce.

examples.text: Сегодня на ужин паста под соусом!
examples.trans: Tonight for dinner we have pasta with sauce!

meanings.en: to put, to place in an upright position
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тавить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to put', forming an aspectual pair with 'поставить'.

examples.trans: Where should I put the plate?
Put the kettle on the table.

examples.text: Успокойтесь, я ещё сделаю! Куда ставить тарелку?
examples.trans: Calm down, I'll make more! Where should I put the plate?

meanings.en: to go and come back, to pop over
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ходить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'ходить'.

examples.trans: Yes, go on.
I'll pop to the shop.
Yes, go on. Don't mix it up with another one!

meanings.note: the comparative 'тише' = quieter, used as 'shh'
тише! (comparative) = quiet! keep it down!

examples.trans: Quiet, the children are asleep!
It's quiet here.

examples.text: Тише, пожалуйста, шеф сейчас разговаривает с важным гостем!
examples.trans: Quieter, please, the chef is speaking with an important guest right now!

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.
Dad is already home.
I'm already home.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'знать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to recognise; to find out', paired with 'узнавать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to find out, to learn') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Did you recognise me?
I'll find out where he is.
You recognised me. Thanks for seeing me.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to stuff, fill (culinary)'.

examples.trans: Stuff the fish with lemon.

examples.text: И фаршируй рыбу жюльеном с лимоном.
examples.trans: And stuff the fish with julienne and lemon.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: Cleverly thought out, boss!
The boss signed the order.
The chef is in the kitchen.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
